stories.title: Solana cuts slot time to 350ms as first governance vote nears
stories.summary: Solana reduced its blockchain slot time to 350 milliseconds, speeding up how fast the network processes transactions. The change lands as Solana approaches its first governance vote. CryptoSlate reported that a live quorum display for the vote showed 60%, but flagged the number as an error.
stories.whyItMatters: Faster slot times may help Solana compete for high-throughput applications, but a broken quorum readout raises doubts about the reliability of its new governance tools.
whatToWatch: Outcome of Solana's first governance vote
Whether the quorum display error gets fixed or explained
Any network performance changes after the slot-time cut
questions: What caused the quorum display error?
Does the faster slot time add new risks to network stability?

sources.title: Solana’s first governance vote nears with a live 60% quorum display error
Solana cuts blockchain slot time to 350 milliseconds

stories.title: SEC floats path for crypto projects to raise $75M and exit securities status
stories.summary: The SEC proposed a rule that would let crypto projects raise up to $75 million and later end their token's status as a securities contract. CryptoSlate reports the proposal would give projects a defined offramp from securities regulation once conditions are met.
stories.whyItMatters: A formal exit from securities status would remove a major legal overhang for token issuers and could reshape how US projects structure fundraising.
whatToWatch: Publication of formal SEC rule text and a comment period
Industry and legal reaction to the $75 million cap
Whether already-trading tokens could qualify
questions: What conditions must a project meet to end securities status?
Would this apply retroactively to tokens already trading?

sources.title: SEC proposes a path for crypto projects to raise $75 million and later end the token’s securities contract

stories.title: MiCA regulators turn attention to DeFi vaults
stories.summary: The EU's MiCA framework is starting to focus on DeFi vaults, Cointelegraph reports. The report says applying securities-style rules to decentralized, code-governed vaults will be technically and legally difficult.
stories.whyItMatters: How MiCA treats DeFi vaults will help decide whether decentralized products can operate legally in the EU or face the same compliance burden as centralized platforms.
whatToWatch: Specific MiCA guidance or enforcement actions on DeFi vaults
Response from vault protocols and their operators
questions: How will regulators identify a responsible party for a decentralized vault?
Will enforcement target front-end operators instead of the underlying protocol?

sources.title: MiCA is coming for DeFi vaults, but regulation will be difficult

stories.title: Crypto's week: bears get squeezed as bitcoin and ether rally, X eyes stablecoin payouts
stories.summary: CoinDesk's weekly roundup says short sellers in bitcoin and ether took heavy losses as a squeeze-led rally pushed prices higher. Separately, Elon Musk's X is reportedly looking at paying creators in stablecoins.
stories.whyItMatters: A squeeze-driven rally reflects trader positioning more than fundamentals, and a platform the size of X adopting stablecoin payouts would mark a real step toward mainstream stablecoin use.
whatToWatch: Whether X confirms or launches stablecoin creator payments
Whether the rally holds once short positions clear out
questions: How much of the rally was short covering versus new buying?
Which stablecoin, and on which chain, would X use?

stories.title: Instant Bitcoin validation would need 17 GPU-years of compute, report finds
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate report estimates that achieving 27-millisecond transaction validation on Bitcoin would take roughly 17 GPU years of compute power. The figure shows the scale of hardware needed for near-instant settlement on Bitcoin's current design.
stories.whyItMatters: The estimate gives a concrete benchmark for judging Bitcoin speed-up proposals against a real technical constraint, rather than marketing claims.
whatToWatch: Any proposals that would cut the compute requirement
Follow-up analysis from other researchers
questions: What assumptions sit behind the 17 GPU-year estimate?
Which project or team is pursuing 27ms validation?

sources.title: Reaching instant 27ms validation on Bitcoin will take 17 GPU years of compute power

stories.title: Riot Platforms may free up 1,500 BTC as rally reverses crash-era pledge
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that a bitcoin price crash had forced miner Riot Platforms to pledge 1,825 BTC, likely as loan collateral. The recent rally may now let Riot release roughly 1,500 BTC of that pledge.
stories.whyItMatters: Miner collateral moves show how leveraged bitcoin holders behave through price swings, and a large unlock can affect coins available to the market.
whatToWatch: Confirmation from Riot on any collateral release
Whether freed BTC is sold or held
questions: What loan or facility required the original pledge?
Would a released 1,500 BTC be sold into the market?

sources.title: Bitcoin crash forced Riot to pledge 1,825 BTC, but this huge rally may now free up 1,500 BTC

stories.title: Illinois rule could hit crypto users with monthly tax bills on total holdings
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that new Illinois rules could require everyday crypto users to pay monthly tax bills based on the total value of their holdings, if their broker fails to collect the tax first.
stories.whyItMatters: Taxing total asset value, rather than gains or transactions, would be a major departure from typical crypto tax treatment and could set a precedent other states watch.
whatToWatch: Which brokers count as 'covered' under the rule
The rule's effective date and any legal challenges
Guidance on how users self-report if a broker doesn't collect
questions: Does the tax apply to unrealized gains or to total value regardless of gains?
How would Illinois enforce this against out-of-state exchanges?

sources.title: Everyday crypto users face monthly tax bills on total asset value if covered brokers fail to collect under new Illinois rules

stories.title: Zcash surges 48% past $800 on Grayscale spot ETF push
stories.summary: Zcash jumped 48% to trade above $800, CoinDesk reports, as a Grayscale push for a spot Zcash ETF fueled speculation the privacy coin could be the 'next bitcoin.'
stories.whyItMatters: A sharp rally tied to ETF speculation, not a fundamental change, is a reminder that filing news can move prices well ahead of any regulatory decision.
whatToWatch: SEC action on a Grayscale spot Zcash ETF
Whether the rally holds or fades
questions: Has Grayscale filed a spot Zcash ETF, or is this speculation about a future filing?
How does Zcash's privacy design affect its ETF approval odds?

stories.title: BitMart weighs partial restart and creditor payouts weeks after shutdown
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports that crypto exchange BitMart is now considering a partial restart of operations and payouts to creditors, weeks after announcing it would shut down.
stories.whyItMatters: A reversal from shutdown to partial restart matters for affected users' odds of recovering funds, and shows how exchange failures can play out.
whatToWatch: A formal announcement on restart scope and timeline
Terms and size of any creditor payouts
questions: Why did BitMart originally shut down, and what changed?
What share of creditors would be made whole?

stories.title: Sandbox halts Base and BNB Chain bridging after exploit
stories.summary: Web3 gaming network The Sandbox has paused bridging on Base and BNB Chain following an exploit, CoinDesk reports.
stories.whyItMatters: Bridge exploits remain one of crypto's most persistent security weak points, and a pause affects users' ability to move assets between chains.
whatToWatch: Sandbox's post-mortem on the exploit's cause and losses
Timeline for restoring bridging
Any reimbursement plan for affected users
questions: How much was lost in the exploit?
Was the vulnerability in Sandbox's own bridge code or a third-party dependency?

stories.title: Tokenized stocks risk a 1960s-style 'paper crisis,' Fairmint CEO warns
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports that Fairmint's CEO warns tokenized stocks could repeat Wall Street's 1960s 'paper crisis,' when back-office paperwork failures nearly broke the settlement system.
stories.whyItMatters: As tokenized equities grow, operational and settlement risk, not just technology, could decide whether the market scales safely.
whatToWatch: Specific back-office or settlement fixes proposed by tokenization platforms
Regulatory scrutiny of tokenized stock infrastructure
questions: What specific operational gaps exist today?
Which platforms are most exposed to this risk?

stories.title: AI is making Bitcoin's software a bigger target, security group says
stories.summary: Decrypt reports that AI tools have made Bitcoin's underlying software a more attractive target for attackers, prompting a group to organize a defense effort.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin's security depends on the integrity of its core software, so a rise in AI-assisted attacks on that code is a systemic risk worth tracking.
whatToWatch: Details on the group's defensive measures
Any disclosed vulnerabilities or attempted exploits
questions: What does the group's defense effort actually involve, such as audits, bounties, or tooling?
Has an AI-assisted attack on Bitcoin software already succeeded?
